Done. I built a faithful before/after reproducer, captured the real race-detector output, applied the return-value fix, and verified it.

## Summary

**Deliverable:** `~/go-data-race-completion-path-global.md`

**Root cause (confirmed by live `-race` output):** A package-level `priceAsOf` string was written inside `computeCostUSD` (invoked by every tick-completion goroutine) and read later at outcome assembly. The trace named `computeCostUSD` on *both sides* of a write/write race and again against `processCompletion`'s read — the classic "same function, package address" signature of an unsynchronized global. The claimed `priceAsOfMu` guard was never locked.

**Fix applied in `~/race-lab/after/tick.go`:**
- Deleted the global and the unused mutex.
- Kept the frozen `computeCostUSD(t Tick) float64` signature, made it pure.
- Added `computeCostUSDWithAsOf(t Tick) (cost float64, priceAsOf string)` as a thin wrapper.
- At the call site: `cost, asOf := computeCostUSDWithAsOf(t)` and set `Outcome.PriceAsOf = asOf`.

**Verification (actual runs):**
- Before: `go test -race -count=1 ./...` → exit 1, 2× `WARNING: DATA RACE`.
- After: `go test -race -count=1 ./...` → `ok tickafter 1.020s`, exit 0.
- Re-ran the exact failing tests by name: both PASS.
- Frozen signature preserved; no package-global references remain.

The document includes the `gh run view <id> --log-failed | grep "WARNING: DATA RACE"` diagnostic path, the full root-cause analysis, the diff, and a reviewer checklist.

signatures.description: Go scheduler: a package-level string global (price-as-of stamp) written inside a cost-computation helper called from every tick-completion goroutine and read at completion-assembly sites -> DATA RACE (CI race job red on 4 runs; failures surface in unrelated concurrent tests). Diagnosis: gh run view <id> --log-failed + grep WARNING: DATA RACE gives the exact write/write stack (same function both sides = unsynchronized global); comment claimed locking that did not exist. Fix that worked: eliminate the global entirely - return the stamp alongside the cost from a thin computeCostUSDWithAsOf wrapper (frozen signature kept), populate the outcome field from the return value at the call sites. Verify: go test -race -count=1 package green + the exact failing tests re-run. Lesson: any value captured on one goroutine and consumed at outcome-assembly must travel as a return value, never via a package global, even when values are identical across goroutines.
